policy_questions.question: The assistant assumes the admin role by default. When does the role of the logged-in user (agent, manager, customer) limit what it may do, and how is that role known?

Do the agent grants include linking or updating case SLAs, sending notifications and deleting case-knowledge links, or are these forbidden to agents? The SLA duties (pause on pending, align an SLA when a case moves to in progress) need SLA tools that the agent and manager grant lists do not name.
Does 'contribute to knowledge management as reviewers' let a manager create or update knowledge articles?

From which states may a case move to canceled? The transition list ends with a bare 'canceled'. Also, do agents only change new → in_progress (Working on a Case), or every transition of the lifecycle list?
No tool takes sys_updated_on. Does the system set it, or must the agent do something?
No tool has a case notes, cause or resolution notes argument. Where must the escalation justification be logged?

The Free form text policies give an escalation reason text ("The case could not be completed on time..."), but the tool accepts only urgency, vip, impact, breach_risk, customer_request. Which one applies?
Does the 30–120 character limit apply to the knowledge article body too?
An article found by automated search that resolves the case: suggested or resolution?
Installed products must be in_use, but only retired / repair are excluded explicitly. May an in_stock installed product be attached to a case?
Security limits updates to cases the user owns, is assigned to or whose group they are in. Does this hold for a manager who reassigns cases across groups, and for the default admin role?
Registering says to collect inputs, but the assistant must not ask the user for information. Must missing inputs come only from the request and the records?
